extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of ancient Athenian political institutions; historians and classicists
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive account of the constitutional organization, offices, selection methods, duties, and legal/procedural standards of classical Athens (Council, Assembly, magistrates, military, markets, and reconciliation terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchise eligibility and enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: The franchise is open to all who are of citizen birth by both parents; they are enrolled among the demesmen at the age of eighteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On enrollment the demesmen vote under oath whether the candidate is of age and freeborn; appeals to law-courts are possible if rejected; if a court decides he has no right to be enrolled he is sold by the state as a slave; if he wins he is enrolled without further question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demesmen and Council oversight of enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council examines those who have been enrolled and, if it finds any less than eighteen, fines the demesmen who enrolled him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a check on improper enrollments and imposes financial penalties on responsible demesmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ephebi appointment, guardianship and training
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of the enrollment examination, fathers appoint three fellow-tribesmen over forty as guardians (one of whom the Assembly elects) and a director; youths (Ephebi) undergo a two-year program of temple circuit, garrison duty, public display of military evolutions, and training in heavy armour, bow, javelin, and catapult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians receive a drachma each, youths four obols; they mess by tribes, are exempt from taxes during service, cannot bring or have actions brought against them (with exceptions for inheritance, wards of state, or sacrificial ceremonies), and receive a shield and spear after the first-year display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of ordinary magistrates by lot
rubrics_metrics.description: All the magistrates concerned with ordinary routine administration are elected by lot, with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions (elected by vote) include the Military Treasurer, Commissioners of the Theoric fund, and Superintendent of Springs; military officers are also elected by vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council of Five Hundred composition and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council of Five Hundred is elected by lot, fifty from each tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each tribe holds the office of Prytanes in turn (order by lot); Prytanes' terms and rotation are specified (first four serve 36 days each, last six 35 days due to lunar reckoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prytanes duties and meeting schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Prytanes convene meetings of the Council and the Assembly; the Council meets every day unless a holiday, the Assembly four times in each prytany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prytanes draw up the programme of Council business and the Assembly; one meeting per prytany is the 'sovereign' Assembly for ratifying magistrates and discussing corn and defence; the sixth prytany handles ostracism consideration and certain complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly business allocation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws require the two remaining Assembly meetings each prytany to deal with three religious questions, three connected with heralds and embassies, and three secular subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes questions are brought forward without a preliminary vote; heralds and envoys appear first before the Prytanes and deliver dispatches to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: President of the Prytanes role and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A single President of the Prytanes is elected by lot to preside for a night and a day; he may not hold the office more than once and cannot hold it twice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He keeps keys and public seal, remains in the Tholus with one-third of the Prytanes named by him, appoints by lot nine Proedri (one from each tribe except the current Prytanes tribe), and from these appoints a President for meetings; Proedri preserve order, decide votings, and may dismiss meetings. No one may act as President more than once in the year; may be Proedrus once per prytany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election procedure for Generals and Hipparch
rubrics_metrics.description: Elections to the offices of General and Hipparch and all other military commands are held in the Assembly after the sixth prytany by the first board of Prytanes in whose term the omens are favorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be a preliminary consideration by the Council before these elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council's loss of punitive powers and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly the Council could inflict fines, imprisonment, and death; after abuses, the Thesmothetae must bring such sentences before the law-courts and the jurors' decision is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This curtails summary powers of the Council and places final jurisdiction with law-courts; private individuals may still lay information against magistrates with appeals to law-courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council's preliminary cognizance of Assembly business
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council takes preliminary cognizance of all matters brought before the Assembly; the Assembly cannot vote on any question unless it has first been considered by the Council and placed on the programme by the Prytanes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person carrying a motion in the Assembly is liable to an action for illegal proposal if these procedures are not followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipbuilding and naval supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council supervises existing triremes with tackle and sheds, builds new triremes or quadriremes as the Assembly votes, appoints master-builders by vote, and for building triremes appoints ten commissioners chosen from its members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If master-builders do not hand over completed work to the next Council, the old Council cannot receive the customary donation normally given during its successor's term; the Council inspects public buildings and can report fraud to the Assembly and law-courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasure and sacred property custody and eligibility for treasurers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten treasurers of Athena are elected by lot, one from each tribe; according to Solon's law they must be Pentacosiomedimni, though in practice the lot-holder holds office even if poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They take charge of statue of Athena, Victory figures, ornaments, and money in the presence of the Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners for Public Contracts (Poletae) duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Poletae (one from each tribe) farm out public contracts, lease mines and taxes in conjunction with the Military Treasurer and Commissioners of the Theoric fund, and sell confiscated property in the presence of the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They enter lease lists on whitened tablets, make separate prytany instalment lists, draw up lists of confiscated farms and dwellings; dwellings' value must be paid in five years, farms in ten; instalments are paid in the ninth prytany; leases of sacred enclosures are brought in by the King-archon on whitened tablets and paid in a prytany that yields largest revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment processing and Receivers-General role
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Receivers-General (Apodectae), elected by lot, receive the tablets and strike off instalments as they are paid in the presence of the Council, returning tablets to the public clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failures to pay are noted on the tablet; the defaulter must pay double deficiency or be imprisoned; the Council has legal power to exact payments and impose imprisonment; apportionment of funds is publicly posted and open to challenge for malpractice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and account-examination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council elects ten Auditors (Logistae) by lot to audit magistrates' accounts each prytany and one Examiner of Accounts (Euthunus) by lot from each tribe with two assessors to receive charges against magistrates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints must be entered within three days of audit on whitened tablets with name of accuser and alleged malpractice and penalty claim; Examiners forward private cases to local justices and public cases to Thesmothetae who may bring accounts before law-courts for final judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and penalties for state horses and cavalry enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council inspects state horses; owners keeping a good horse in bad condition are mulcted in corn allowance; poor horses are branded with a wheel on the jaw and disqualified; those rejected for cavalry service are deprived of their horse or pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roll of cavalry is drawn by Commissioners of Enrolment elected by open vote; sealed tablet of cavalry names is opened before the Council; affidavits of physical or pecuniary incapacity can remove persons; the Council votes on suitability where no affidavit is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public building contracts adjudication (jury by lot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly the Council decided plans and contracts for public buildings and the robe of Athena; now this work is done by a jury in the law-courts appointed by lot because the Council had shown favouritism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an institutional reform to reduce corruption/favouritism in public contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision of manufacture of festival prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council shares with the Military Treasurer the superintendence of manufacture of the images of Victory and prizes at the Panathenaic festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects joint oversight of ceremonial/state property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for infirm paupers
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons possessing less than three minas who are crippled and unable to work are, after examination by the Council, to receive two obols a day from the state for their support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A treasurer is appointed by lot to attend to them; Council conducts examination to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners for Repairs of Temples funding and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Commissioners for Repairs of Temples, elected by lot, receive a sum of thirty minas from the Receivers-General to carry out necessary repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation and use of funds for temple maintenance is centralized under these commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: City Commissioners (Astynomi) public-order duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten City Commissioners, five for Piraeus and five for the city, enforce public-order regulations: limit hiring fees for female musicians to two drachmas (use lot if multiple hirers), prevent sewage discharge within ten stradia of walls, stop street obstructions (buildings, barriers, mid-air drain-pipes, doors opening outwards), and remove corpses using state slaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad municipal regulatory role covering public health, traffic/access, and funerary management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market and weights & measures oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Market Commissioners (Agoranomi) ensure articles for sale are pure and unadulterated; Commissioners of Weights and Measures (Metronomi) ensure fair weights and measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both offices are elected by lot (five for Piraeus and five for the city for each office) and set and enforce market quality and standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corn Commissioners' price and weight regulation duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Corn Commissioners (Sitophylaces) ensure unprepared corn is offered at reasonable prices, millers sell barley meal at proportionate prices to barley, bakers sell loaves proportionate to wheat price and at weights fixed by Commissioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers adjusted over time (formerly ten; later twenty for city and fifteen for Piraeus); Commissioners fix standard weight and regulate market prices tied to raw grain costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superintendents of the Mart duty for grain supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Superintendents of the Mart are to superintend the Mart and compel merchants to bring two-thirds of the corn which is brought by sea to the Corn Mart into the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures adequate urban grain stocks and prevents external hoarding or diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of reconciliation and amnesty after civil strife
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconciliation terms: secessionists to settle at Eleusis with full civil rights and self-government, temple common ground, restrictions on entering Athens except during mysteries, obligation to pay their share to common defence, assistance in purchasing houses or valuation by three valuers on each side, lists and departure deadlines (list within ten days after oaths, departure within twenty days), and restriction on holding Athens office until reregistered as resident; general amnesty for past events except the Thirty, the Ten, the Eleven, and magistrates in Piraeus unless they submit accounts in the usual way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magistrates in Piraeus give accounts before court of citizens rated in Piraeus; city magistrates before those rated in the city; on these terms secession may proceed; each party repays its own wartime debts separately (though Athenians repaid borrowed money of the Thirty to restore harmony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trials for homicide and ancestral legal practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials for homicide, including all cases where one party had killed or wounded another, should be conducted according to ancestral practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves customary procedures for the gravest criminal cases rather than ad hoc or novel processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers and procedures of the Eleven regarding prisoners and confiscated property
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eleven, appointed by lot, take care of prisoners in state gaol; thieves, kidnappers, and pickpockets if pleading guilty are executed by them; if they deny charges the Eleven bring them before law-courts; if acquitted they are released; otherwise executed. The Eleven also present lists of farms and houses claimed as state property to law-courts and deliver properties to the Commissioners for Public Contracts when decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines custodial, prosecutorial referral, and property-administration functions with reliance on law-courts for disputed cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on publication and timing of lists for secession and civic actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of seceding persons must be made within ten days after oaths for those already present and departure within twenty days; persons abroad receive same terms after return; lists of instalments, leases, and seized property are recorded on whitened tablets and handled on specified prytany schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies tight deadlines and written record-keeping procedures to govern secession, fiscal instalments, leases, and confiscations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory public account submission by certain magistrates
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain magistrates (including those in Piraeus and other named boards) are excluded from general amnesty unless they submit their accounts in the usual way before the appropriate court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures financial accountability as precondition for clemency; accounts are judged by courts of citizens rated in the relevant district (Piraeus or city).
